rounds.text: QMS Medical Allied Services Ltd is significantly under-appreciated by the market, trading at an EV/EBITDA of 14.25x against a sector benchmark of 16.23x and a P/E of 28.54x below its sector benchmark of 30.64x [E6, E11]. The underlying business quality is robust, highlighted by a strong cash conversion of 1.58x where reported profits are fully backed by operating cash flow, alongside zero capital-work-in-progress indicating that new capacity has come online [E24, E30]. Management maintains strong revenue visibility, guiding for a total top line of around INR 220 crores, supported by an expanding products business and a proprietary technology platform that serves over 1 million patients across 100-plus programs [E69, E72, E77]. Institutional confidence is building with domestic institutions increasing their holding to 1.30% alongside positive money flow signals, reinforced by a sector tailwind score of nearly 1.0 [E33, E34, E63]. Conceded: the company faces a negative trailing profit growth of -19% and a decrease in promoter holding over the last three years [E15, E52]. Nevertheless, consolidated EBITDA grew 27% year-on-year to INR 8.3 crores with margins improving to 14.6%, proving that operational execution remains strong [E74].

The evidence reveals that QMS Medical Allied Services Ltd carries significant valuation and operational risks that are currently unsupported by its underlying financial performance [E61]. A discounted cash flow model values the intrinsic price at Rs 129 against a market price of Rs 169, leaving a negative margin of safety of -30.8% [E35, E36]. Furthermore, the reverse DCF indicates that the current market price demands an aggressive 13.7% earnings growth, which outpaces the 10.0% assumed in the base case [E37]. Operational headwinds are also apparent, as compounded profit growth over the trailing twelve months dropped by -19% [E15], and quarterly operating margins contracted by 3 percentage points to 12% in Sep 2026 compared to the previous year [E21]. Additionally, insider commitment appears to be waning, with promoter holdings declining by 5.56 percentage points from 73.67% in Dec 2022 to 68.11% in Sep 2026 [E31]. Conceded: the company demonstrates a strong short-term price return of 74% over 1 year [E17] and positive institutional money flow [E34].

Conceded: [E35, E36]. While the DCF and reverse DCF suggest the price demands 13.7% earnings growth against a 10.0% base case [E37], those models ignore tangible operational catalysts and strong cash generation [E26]. The assertion regarding a 19% drop in trailing profit growth [E15] is offset by consolidated EBITDA growing 27% year-on-year to INR8.3 crores with margins improving to 14.6% [E74], driven by higher service revenue contributions [E75]. The quarterly operating margin contraction [E21] is temporary noise against management's solid top-line guidance of around INR220 crores for the total top line [E69] and clear visibility of INR100 crores to INR105 crores in net overall contribution to PSP with operations revenue in FY27 [E68]. Regarding waning promoter holding [E31], this slight reduction is actively counterbalanced by positive institutional money flow and increasing domestic institutional participation from 0.00% to 1.30% [E33, E34].

Conceded: [E74]. The bull relies heavily on management's guided top-line of INR220 crores [E69] and service visibility [E67], yet actual trailing performance shows compounded profit growth contracting by -19% [E15] alongside a quarterly operating margin drop of 3 percentage points in September 2026 [E21]. Dismissing this margin contraction as temporary noise ignores the rules-based screen which flags earnings growth as decelerating [E59] and net profit down -32% year-on-year [E58]. Furthermore, while the bull minimizes the drop in promoter holding from 73.67% down to 68.11% [E31], this insider divestment compounds the valuation risk of holding a stock trading at 3.59x book value [E7] while facing a negative -30.8% margin of safety on DCF terms [E36]. The claim of increasing domestic institutional participation [E33] cannot mask the broader reality of foreign institutions pulling back their holdings [E32] and a high annualised volatility of 61.5% [E44].

evidence.quote: Our Products business continued to demonstrate healthy traction, supported by our expanding distribution network, Q-Devices portfolio and presence across QMSMEDS, e-Grameen and other digital platforms.

evidence.quote: The margin increase is driven by the shift of our revenue from the revenue contribution; a higher contribution is coming from services. So that is a driver for the expansion of gross margins.

evidence.quote: So, our PSPs are typically cost-plus contracts. So, the employee cost plus the administration cost, plus cost of other allied services are charged to the client, and we have a markup. And PSPs typically work on an annual contract basis.
